The core gameplay is still solid, but it's increasingly difficult to justify investing time in a game whose developers seem to prioritise revenue over actually improving the player experience.

[h1]⚠️ PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS – NOT RECOMMENDED[/h1]

[hr]

[h2]Too Many Cheaters. Not Enough Action.[/h2]

Honestly, PUBG is becoming increasingly frustrating to play because of the ridiculous number of cheaters.

[b]Aimbots, wallhacks, suspicious players and blatant cheating[/b] are ruining match after match. You spend time looting, positioning yourself, and playing strategically, only to get killed by someone who seems to know exactly where you are or never misses a shot.

What's the point of playing a competitive battle royale when legitimate players are constantly punished for playing fair?

[hr]

[h2]What Needs to Change:[/h2]

[list]
[*]Better anti-cheat protection.
[*]Permanent bans for confirmed cheaters.
[*]Faster action against reported players.
[*]More protection for legitimate players.
[*]Less focus on cosmetics and more focus on fixing the game.
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Final Verdict[/h2]

PUBG has the potential to be an amazing game, but the cheating problem makes it difficult to enjoy.

I'm tired of wasting time in matches ruined by cheaters. Players deserve a fair competitive experience.

[b][color=#ff3333]NOT RECOMMENDED.[/color][/b]

[i]Too many cheaters. Too little action. Enough is enough.[/i]

After 1,200+ Hours of PUBG, Here’s My Honest Review.

First of all, PUBG is genuinely one of the greatest battle royale games I’ve ever played. The excitement, intense battles, and competitive atmosphere are incredible. From the early days until now, PUBG has delivered unforgettable moments and continues to be an amazing game.

However, there is one major problem that is slowly destroying everything that makes this game enjoyable: CHEATERS.

Despite constant updates, anti-cheat improvements, and the countless reports submitted by players, hackers are still ruining matches.

Let me give you a realistic example:

Imagine spending an entire match fighting, surviving, and doing everything you can to reach the final five players. You’re incredibly close to winning.

Then suddenly, one player starts eliminating everyone with suspicious precision. He instantly knows where players are hiding, locks onto one target, kills them, immediately switches to another, and repeats the process until everyone is dead.

It’s as if he’s using ESP/Wallhack to locate players and Aimbot to eliminate them effortlessly.

Now imagine being one of those players who spent the entire match carefully surviving, only to lose against someone who appears to be using cheats.

Where is the fairness? Where is the competition? And most importantly, where is the fun?

We don’t expect to win every match. Losing against a genuinely skilled player is completely acceptable. That’s part of the excitement of PUBG.

But losing to someone using cheats after putting in so much effort is incredibly frustrating.

After more than 1,200 hours, I can confidently say that PUBG itself isn’t the problem. The game is fantastic. The real problem is the cheaters who are destroying the experience for legitimate players.

I sincerely hope the developers make anti-cheat enforcement a much higher priority, improve detection systems, and take stronger action against reported cheaters.

PUBG is an incredible game, but even the greatest game loses its magic when fair competition disappears.

This is my honest opinion after 1,200+ hours of gameplay.

Not recommended right now, because of constant crashes and freezes on PC.

I played PUBG from December 2025 to June 2026 with no problems on the same PC. After I reinstalled in September (Update 43.1), the game started crashing in the lobby and in matches, and it has continued through every update since. After the latest 13 GB update (build 2610.1.1.57) I can barely open the game. It either crashes or freezes on the loading screen.

The crash dumps show the game's own code (TslGame.exe) reading invalid memory. The same bad address shows up on three different builds, so it looks like a bug in the game, not my PC.

I tried a fresh Windows install, many GPU drivers, DX11 and DX12, a different drive, overlays off, and a memory test. Nothing fixed it. PUBG support told me it's a game bug and to wait for an update, but the update didn't fix it.

PC: i3-7100, GTX 1050 Ti, 12 GB RAM.

I'll change this review once the crashes are fixed. Until then I can't recommend it.
